No single channel dominates the move, so this is not about one channel's ad spend or search ranking — look for something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -9.6% does not match new subs +2.7% from 7 days earlier — this drop is not coming from new customers.
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 09-08 vs 09-01 is -9.6%, but App Total New Subs on 09-01 vs 08-25 was +2.7% — they moved in opposite directions. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. Since those subs went the other way, this drop is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YCP is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-4.4% vs Install +2.7%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YCP New Subs -4.4% vs Install +2.7% (worse than its installs); YCV New Subs -5.1% vs Install +4.9% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Revenue -3.1% is mostly YCV — not every app.
insights.body: App Total Revenue moved -3.1% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -3.1%, YMK -0.6%, YCP -2.4%, YCV -8.4%). YCV accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total New Subs (+5.1% vs -7.6%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total New Subs in US is +5.1% while all countries together are -7.6% — a gap of +12.7pp. US is about 38% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Market trend — DE is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-14.1%, now 14.0%).
insights.body: In DE, 14.0% of installs now turn into new subs — -14.1% versus last period. It is about 6% of revenue (a market worth watching): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Best and worst markets — GB turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (22.4% vs 11.6% overall).
insights.body: In GB, 22.4% of installs turn into new subs, versus 11.6% across all markets and apps (+10.8pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. GB is about 5% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is -23.5% this period.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting toward Paid Install (+7.3% vs -0.1% for installs overall).
insights.body: Paid Install was 13,297, +7.3% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved -0.1% — a difference of +7.4 percentage points. Paid Install is now 45.7% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.

insights.title: Next period outlook — No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is -7.6% and App Total Install is -0.1%; the gap between them (-7.5pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.
